target_customer: Women shopping online for dresses who struggle with fit
problem: Women find it hard to buy dresses online that fit their body, leading to returns. Fit to Form suggested dresses that women with similar body types had reviewed positively.
business_model: E-commerce, probably affiliate or retail margin (not stated)
product_category: Body type based dress shopping site

founders.name: Radha Jain
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page without a bio.

founders.name: Genevieve Payzer
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page without a bio.

competitors.name: Fovo
competitors.what: Shop by body shape not size, using a five question quiz

competitors.name: Savitude
competitors.what: SaaS tool for retailers matching clothes to body shape using IBM Watson visual recognition

technical_complexity.rationale: A recommendation site over reviews and measurements is standard web engineering; the hard parts are data and merchandising.

defensibility.rationale: Several body shape shopping tools already existed and none shows a data or network moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying it directly; the site appears to have stopped operating without a public announcement.

market_need_then: Fit related returns were a known apparel e-commerce pain, and earlier startups (Fovo 2016, Savitude 2017, Fitbay 2014) targeted body shape matching, which shows persistent but contested demand.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand pages found; the descriptive name competes with many fit and form brands.

outcome_analysis: Fit to Form was a two person San Francisco team in YC Summer 2019 building a dress shopping site that matched women by body type. YC lists it inactive, and a low quality directory says it failed on operating costs and scale, which no better source confirms. The cause is not public, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: thefittoform.com returned HTTP 503, so the site is treated as unreachable and not confirmed dead. The 150K seed rests on a single aggregator (Village) with no date and is probably the standard YC deal. Crunchbase shows little. Altss lists S19 while Crustdata lists W20; the directory says Summer 2019. The Loot-Drop claim about operating costs is a weak single source and is not used for failure factors. Fovo and Savitude sources are dated before the batch; traction and funding were not in the snippets.
